contributions.statement: When measuring review of agent-authored PRs across hosts, count the developer who invoked the agent as the author, not as an independent reviewer, because with that definition 40.1% of agent PRs vs 21.5% of human PRs get no independent review, and trend directions flip under other defensible definitions.
contributions.evidence: §II-B, §IV text near Fig. 1 and Appendix 1: paired Wilcoxon on per-project author-only share, k=1,553, p<0.001, r=0.42; authors show direction flips across operationalizations.

contributions.statement: Tier human approval of agent PRs by risk (contract/schema changes) rather than applying a blanket review gate.
contributions.evidence: Proposition P17 from practitioner quotes; untested, and the authors state they confirm none of the relationships.

reason: The theory is untested practitioner opinion, but the motivating mining result gives a concrete, measured rule for defining review independence in agent-PR metrics.
